messages:
samantha: Heads-up: seeing a 3x tail latency spike for a private/VPC customer in us-west-2 starting ~09:10 UTC. Affects mv2-quant-llama route on dedicated pool-c. Traces show kernel selection flipped to fallback kernel on a subset of nodes and KV cache hit rate dropped from ~92% -> ~40% at the same time.

josh: Oof. Any obvious egress errors in the node logs? conntrack?

samantha: checking logs now. I see a bunch of short TCP retransmits and a rise in ip_conntrack entries. Also some MTU-related fragmentation in tcpdump on the egress ENI.

priyanka: Can you paste the perf sample and the kernel selector decision blob? Might be related to quantized-kernel thresholds.

samantha: paste below. Perf shows ramp in kernel fallback invocations and one node showing much higher syscall time in sendmsg.

```
# bpftrace snapshot (truncated)
@sendmsg_latency[comm] = hist(lineno);
node-12: sendmsg 99th=220ms -> before was 35ms
kvcache: hit_rate 0.4
kernel_selector: selected=fallback-kernel reason=frag_forced_by_mtu
```

liam: That "frag_forced_by_mtu" flag is new in the kernel heuristics — it triggers when path MTU discovery sees repeated frag failures so we revert to a safer kernel which unfortunately loses some optimized vector kernels.

marco: I suspect this is a VPC egress path issue. We've seen hairpin/NAT MTU clamping on the customer's FW appliances before. If packets are being fragmented, our optimized kernels (which assume contiguous big frames for NVLink copies) degrade.

josh: @samantha can you run `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` and `ip -s link show dev eth0` on the affected node? Also dump iptables POSTROUTING NAT rules.

samantha: Run results:
```
# on node-12
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count = 65534
ip -s link show eth0: mtu 1500 qlen 1000 RX: 24k pkts
iptables -t nat -L POSTROUTING -nv:
Chain POSTROUTING (policy ACCEPT 0 packets, 0 bytes)
 pkts bytes target     prot opt in     out     source               destination
 100K  12M MASQUERADE  all  --  *      eth0    10.0.0.0/8            0.0.0.0/0
```

priyanka: conntrack_count near nf_conntrack_max (65536?) — we might be saturating conntrack which causes drops and retransmits. That explains throughput drop and latency.

infra-bot: [alert] conntrack high watermark on node-12 (65534/65536). Suggested action: increase nf_conntrack_max or reduce short-lived connection rate.

liam: Temp mitigations: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max to 262144, 2) enable net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established tweaks, 3) investigate NAT device for MTU clamp. But changing conntrack on prod needs ops signoff.

marco: Also check if the customer's firewall is doing TCP MSS clamping to 1400 or lower — that can force fragmentation deeper in stack.

samantha: ran a quick `tcpdump -i eth0 -vv 'icmp[0] == 3'` and saw "frag needed and DF set" messages from a hop inside customer network. So PMTU failure upstream.

josh: That matches the kernel_selector reason. When PMTU fails we fall back to safer kernel path which is slower and disables some batching heuristics. Two correlated effects: more small fragments -> KV cache alignment change -> hit rate drops -> increased CPU per token -> higher latency.

priyanka: Action plan: (A) open ticket with customer infra to resolve PMTU/hairpin egress (MSS clamping). (B) short-term: roll cluster pool-c to previous kernel selector config (pin to optimized-kernel) for the affected nodes while we mitigate egress, (C) raise nf_conntrack_max as stopgap and enable conntrack garbage collection tuning.

samantha: I've started canary rollback to pin kernel selector on 3 nodes (node-10..12) back to optimized-kernel and reduced conntrack pressure with `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`.

```
# quick commands used
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/8 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```

devops-bot: deploy  -> canary rollback of kernel-selector config to optimized-kernel on pool-c nodes 10-12 started (run-id: cb-2026-03-18-09:28).

liam: Once canary is in, measure KV cache hit rate and 95/99p tail. If they improve -> rollout. If not, revert and escalate to infra.

marco: Also add a short-term runtime guard: if KV cache hit rate falls >30% for 2m, revert kernel selection for that node automatically. Might avoid manual triage next time.

priyanka: Good idea. Add tracing tag so we can correlate kernel-selection flips with conntrack/mtu events for future postmortem.

samantha: Update: after canary rollback hit rate climbed to 88% and p95 dropped from 220ms -> 45ms on those nodes. Still seeing a few retransmits upstream until customer fixes PMTU.

josh: Nice. Please open an incident ticket with _customer_ contact + network traceroutes attached and request they check MSS/clamping on their firewall/NAT. Add remediation steps we used.

samantha: Opening ticket now and pinging account team. Adding postmortem notes for kernel selector and KV cache sensitivity to MTU-induced fragmentation.

priyanka: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: ticket to customer, infra review for NAT/MTU guidance in our private deployment runbook, and runtime guard for automatic kernel revert. :thumbsup:

samantha: filing the incident and will add measurements/graphs. Closing thread for now unless we see reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
